newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Cholera kills two Rwanda refugees in Zaire village.
newsitem.headline: Cholera kills two Rwanda refugees in Zaire village.

text.p: Cholera has broken out among 120,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees crowded round the Zairean forest village of Tingi-Tingi, killing at least two people, according to the World Health Organisation representative in Kinshasa.
"The WHO informs the international community that a cholera epidemic has broken out in Tingi-Tingi since January 10," Doctor Abdou Moudi told Reuters late on Saturday.
He said 56 cases had been registered in the village, which is 180 km (120 miles) southeast of the regional capital Kisangani on the road to the battlefront with Tutsi-led rebels in the east.
Samples collected by the Medecins Sans Frontieres relief group had been tested in Paris and Kinshasa and proved positive, he added.

Most of the refugees fled to Tingi-Tingi to escape the rebel advance in the east, where their traditional Tutsi rivals hold former refugee towns. Zairean authorities have prevented refugees advancing to Kisangani itself.
Tingi-Tingi has little fresh water and witnesses say hygiene conditions are deplorable. The refugees have little food.
The Zairean army, driven back in disarray by the rebels late last year, has made Kisangani a base for a promised counter-attack.
